info.name: Seatiks Seller API
info.description:
The Seatiks Seller API lets brokers and point-of-sale systems manage their Seatiks inventory
programmatically: search events, create and update listings in bulk, receive sales through signed
webhooks, deliver tickets and read their wallet.

**Authentication.** Every request carries an API key, created in *Settings → Developers*:
`Authorization: Bearer stk_live_…` (or the `X-Api-Key` header). Keys carry scopes; a request that
needs a scope the key does not have fails with `403 insufficient_scope`.

**Live access.** Test keys are available to every verified seller. Live keys (`stk_live_…`) and live
webhook endpoints are granted on request: send a request from *Settings → Developers*, our team
reviews it and replies by email. Until access is granted, and if it is later removed, live calls
fail with `403 live_access_required`.

**Sandbox.** Keys starting with `stk_test_` run against an isolated sandbox: same endpoints, same
shapes, but a fictional event catalog (stable ids from `900000000001`, dates always 3 to 180 days
ahead, full section maps). Listings are never published to any marketplace and nothing touches your
wallet. Use `POST /v1/sandbox/sales` to simulate a sale and receive the webhook.

**Errors.** Every error has the shape `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details"? }, "request_id" }`.
Quote `request_id` (also in the `X-Request-Id` header) when contacting support.

**Rate limits.** 300 requests per minute per key, 600 per account, 30 bulk operations per minute per
account. Responses carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`,
`X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`; a `429` carries `Retry-After`.

**Pagination.** List endpoints return `{ object: "list", data, has_more, next_cursor }`. Pass
`next_cursor` back as `cursor` to fetch the next page.

**Webhooks.** Seatiks POSTs events to your HTTPS endpoint, signed with
`Seatiks-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>` where `hex = HMAC_SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>")`. Reject
events older than 5 minutes. Retries use exponential backoff for about 10 hours; events may arrive
more than once and out of order, so deduplicate on the event `id` and read the sale's `status`.

exec: if (pm.response.code >= 400) pm.test('error envelope', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.error.code).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(b.request_id).to.be.a('string'); });

item.name: Describe the API key in use

request.description: Describe the API key in use

Your team members

The members (sub-sellers) of your team, by name — the choices of the dashboard's "Member"
filter. Use their `id` in `member=` on `GET /v1/listings` and `GET /v1/sales`, and to read
the `member` of a listing or a sale. Your own listings and sales are `owner`.

Available to the account owner, and to a team member who sees all the team's listings or
sales, with a key that has `listings:read` or `sales:read`. A member who only sees their own
gets `403 forbidden`.

query.description: Case-insensitive match on the event name.

request.description:
Search upcoming events

Requires `events:read`. Only events with `listable: true` accept listings. With a `stk_test_` key, returns the fictional sandbox catalog only.

exec: const e = (pm.response.json().data || []).find((x) => x.listable); if (e && !pm.collectionVariables.get('eventId')) pm.collectionVariables.set('eventId', e.id);

item.name: Get an event and its section catalog

request.description:
Get an event and its section catalog

The `sections[].key` values are what `section` expects when creating a listing. With a `stk_test_` key, only sandbox catalog ids (from `900000000001`) exist; any other id returns 404.

item.name: Restrictions, features and benefits — the accepted ids

request.description:
Restrictions, features and benefits — the accepted ids

The only values accepted in a listing's `restrictions`, `features` and `benefits`: send the
`id`s, never free text (an unknown id returns `422 validation_failed`). These are the options of
the dashboard listing form; the `label` is what buyers see. Ids never change. Any valid key can
read this catalog.

Marketplaces — the accepted ids

The marketplaces a listing can be published on: the options of the dashboard listing form, with
the same names. Send their `id`s in a listing's `platforms`. Omitting `platforms` publishes on all
of them, like the form.

- `bundled_with`: the marketplaces published together with this one, as one block. Select all of
  them or none of them: selecting only some returns `422 validation_failed`.
- `available: false`: your account cannot publish there (seller level). Selecting it returns
  `422 validation_failed`.

Any valid key can read this catalog.

query.description: `owner`, or a member `id` from GET /v1/team: only what they created (the dashboard's "Member" filter). A member who only sees their own can only pass their own id.

request.description:
List your listings

Requires `listings:read`. Newest first.

Create listings in bulk (up to 500)

Requires `listings:write`. The whole batch is validated first: any invalid item fails the request
with `422 validation_failed` and per-item `details.items[]`, and nothing is created.

Each item is then processed independently; the response reports one result per input `index`:
`created`, `duplicate` (same idempotency key as an earlier call, the existing listing is
returned), `pending_approval` (your account or the event requires manual approval) or `error`.
A very large batch that runs out of time reports its remaining items as `error` with code
`timeout`: send them again with the same idempotency keys.

**Idempotency.** Set `idempotency_key` on each item, or an `Idempotency-Key` header for the
batch (item keys are derived from it). Retrying with the same keys never creates duplicates.

**Proof of purchase.** Until your account has 5 sales, each listing needs a proof of purchase,
which the API cannot send: such items come back `error` with code `rejected`. List from the
dashboard until then.

**Sections.** Use a section key from `GET /v1/events/{id}`, or a category id alone for a whole
category. Sections removed from the event's map are refused (`rejected`); a listing already on
one keeps it.

Batches of 5 or more are published to marketplaces asynchronously: poll the listing's
`publish_status` / `distribution`.

exec: const d = (pm.response.json().data || []).find((x) => x.listing); if (d) pm.collectionVariables.set('listingId', d.listing.id);

request.description:
Update up to 100 listings

Requires `listings:write`. Each item is `{ id, ...fields }` with the same fields as `PATCH /v1/listings/{id}`.
Get a listing

Update a listing

Requires `listings:write`. Changing an inventory field (`quantity`, `first_seat`, `section`, `row`)
requires `expected_inventory_version` equal to the listing's current `inventory_version`: a sale
may have just decremented it. On mismatch the API answers `409 listing_changed` with
`details.current_inventory_version`; reload and retry. Price-only changes need no version.

`platforms` is checked before anything is changed, then applied after the other fields, one
marketplace at a time: this is not atomic. If it does not fully go through, the API answers
`502 platform_update_failed` with `details.fields_saved` (the other fields were saved) and
`details.platforms` (`[{platform, action, status: done | failed | not_attempted}]`). Read the
listing before retrying: its `inventory_version` may have changed.

item.name: Get the pre-uploaded tickets of a listing

request.description:
Get the pre-uploaded tickets of a listing

Requires `delivery:write`. Tickets uploaded in advance on a listing are delivered automatically as
soon as it sells (instant delivery). A `Mobile Link/PKPASS` listing holds links, any other listing
holds files; `expected` is the listing's quantity.

item.name: Pre-upload ticket files on a listing

request.description:
Pre-upload ticket files on a listing

Requires `delivery:write`. One `files` part per ticket (real PDF, PNG, JPEG or PKPASS files, 20 per
request). Never more files than the listing's quantity, across all requests. Uploading tickets turns
`instant_delivery` on; it is not a setting of its own.
Not for `Mobile Link/PKPASS` listings (`409 wrong_delivery_method`: send links instead). While a buyer
is checking out the listing, its tickets are locked (`409 listing_on_hold`).
Files are sent one by one: if one is refused, the error's `details.uploaded` lists those already
stored and `details.not_sent` those not sent.

item.name: Set the pre-uploaded ticket links of a listing

request.description:
Set the pre-uploaded ticket links of a listing

Requires `delivery:write`. For `Mobile Link/PKPASS` listings only. The list you send REPLACES the
listing's links: HTTPS links, one per ticket, or `{ ios, android }` pairs (not mixed), at most the
listing's quantity. An empty list removes every link. Links turn `instant_delivery` on; an empty lot
turns it off. Locked while a buyer is checking out the listing (`409 listing_on_hold`).

Simulate a sale (test keys only)

Requires `listings:write`. Sells tickets from one of your sandbox listings and emits `sale.created` to your test endpoints. At most 100 simulated sales per hour.

query.description: `owner`, or a member `id` from GET /v1/team: only what they created (the dashboard's "Member" filter). A member who only sees their own can only pass their own id.
Only the sales from this marketplace: a `marketplace` value as it appears on your sales (case-insensitive). A name that matches none of your sales returns an empty list.

request.description:
List your sales

Requires `sales:read`. Newest first. Prefer webhooks for real-time updates.
Get a sale

Update a sale

Requires `delivery:write`. The fields the Sales page of the dashboard lets you change, with the same rules:
- `face_value` (and `face_value_currency`, only together with `face_value`): any time;
- `transfer_method`: only while the sale is `awaiting_delivery` or `awaiting_retransfer` and not under
  review (`409 ticket_type_locked`). The new ticket type is also sent to the marketplace the sale comes
  from; if it refuses, nothing changes for that field (`marketplace_rejected`);
- `internal_note`: any time, `null` or `""` clears it.
A sale handed to the replacement team cannot be edited until the case is closed
(`409 sale_with_replacement_team`). These locks are checked before anything is written.
Fields already equal to the sale's values are skipped. Each field is saved on its own: if one fails,
the error's `details.applied` lists the fields that were saved and `details.failed` the others.

item.name: See what was delivered for a sale

request.description:
See what was delivered for a sale

Requires `delivery:write` (a read-only key cannot fetch tickets). The ticket files, links and
transfer proofs delivered for this sale, as shown on the sale in the dashboard. Each file comes with a
`download_url` valid for `download_urls_expire_in` seconds: call again for fresh links. After a
re-delivery the first delivery is kept: `uploaded_at` tells them apart. Nothing delivered yet: empty lists.

Upload ticket files

Requires `delivery:write`. For E-ticket / Mobile Screenshot sales (`409 wrong_delivery_method` for a
Mobile Link/PKPASS or transfer sale). One `files` part per ticket (PDF, PNG, JPEG or PKPASS, 10 MB max, 20 files
per request, `Content-Length` required);
`files[]` / `files[0]`, `files[1]`… are accepted too (PHP curl).
When the sale has as many files as tickets, Seatiks delivers them to the buyer's marketplace and
the sale becomes `delivered` (you also receive `sale.delivered`). If you split a sale's files over
several requests, send them **one after the other**, never in parallel.
Re-delivery (sale `awaiting_retransfer`): send the new files, in several requests if needed; once
as many new files as tickets are uploaded, the sale becomes `delivered` again.

Deliver mobile ticket links

Requires `delivery:write`. For `Mobile Link/PKPASS` sales only (`409 wrong_delivery_method` otherwise). HTTPS links, at most one per ticket, or `{ ios, android }` pairs. Some marketplaces only accept pairs; a single link is then refused (`400 invalid_request`, send `{ ios, android }` objects). The sale becomes `delivered`.

item.name: Confirm a transfer with its proof

request.description:
Confirm a transfer with its proof

Requires `delivery:write`. For sales whose `transfer_method` is `External Transfer`, `Paper` or
`Local Delivery`: you transferred or handed over the tickets outside Seatiks, and you prove it.
Send **one** proof as a `files` part (screenshot of the completed transfer, or delivery document: PDF,
PNG or JPEG, **700 KB max** — compress screenshots to JPEG, e.g. 1600 px wide, quality 80; each proof
triggers a delivery to the marketplace). Some marketplaces only take images: a PDF may be refused
with `400`. `transfer_source` (the platform the tickets were transferred from) is required for an
`External Transfer`; some marketplaces refuse `Other` with `400`: send the actual platform. The proof
is forwarded to the buyer's marketplace and the sale becomes
`delivered`. Other sales return `409 wrong_delivery_method`: deliver them with `/delivery/files`
or `/delivery/links`.

Read your balances

Requires `wallet:read`. Read-only; withdrawals require the dashboard (two-factor step-up).
List wallet transactions

List webhook endpoints

Requires `webhooks:manage` (account owner keys only). Endpoints belong to the key's mode.

Create a webhook endpoint

The signing `secret` is returned only in this response (and on rotation). Store it. Requires `webhooks:manage` **and** `sales:read`: an endpoint receives every sale of the account, buyer details included. With an API key, only **test** endpoints can be created: a live endpoint is created from the dashboard (Settings → Developers), with two-factor authentication (`403 dashboard_required`).
Get a webhook endpoint

Update a webhook endpoint

Set `enabled` to `true` to re-enable an endpoint disabled after repeated failures. Changing `url` also requires the `sales:read` scope. With an API key, only **test** endpoints can be changed: a live endpoint (it receives buyer details) is changed, re-enabled or disabled from the dashboard, with two-factor authentication (`403 dashboard_required`).

Rotate the signing secret

For 24 hours events carry two `v1=` signatures (new and old secret) so you can deploy the new secret without downtime. Send `{ "expire_previous": true }` to revoke the old secret immediately (e.g. after a leak). The secret of a **live** endpoint is rotated from the dashboard, with two-factor authentication (`403 dashboard_required` with an API key).

Send a test event now

At most 5 test events per minute per endpoint.
List recent deliveries

Redeliver a failed event

Only deliveries in `failed` status, at most 3 manual retries per delivery. Requires `webhooks:manage` and `sales:read`.

Delete up to 500 listings

Requires `listings:write`. Per-id status: `deleted`, `not_found`, `pending` (unpublished now,
removal from a marketplace still in progress) or `error` (code `listing_on_hold` when a buyer
currently holds the listing; the other ids are still deleted).

Delete a listing

Requires `listings:write`. A listing currently held by a buyer cannot be deleted:
`409` with code `listing_on_hold`.

Remove a pre-uploaded ticket file

Requires `delivery:write`. Removing the last file turns `instant_delivery` off. Locked while a buyer is
checking out the listing (`409 listing_on_hold`).

Delete a webhook endpoint

With an API key, only **test** endpoints can be deleted: a live endpoint is deleted from the dashboard, with two-factor authentication (`403 dashboard_required`).
